findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "filter_properties" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: filter_properties, get_property, search, find_entity_owner, motivated_sellers_near · Private data: get_property, search_properties, find_owner_portfolio, search, fetch, find_entity_owner, motivated_sellers_near, draft_offer_letter · Public sink: get_market_stats, find_entity_owner · Destructive: list_saved_filters, get_usage.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: filter_properties, get_property, search, find_entity_owner, motivated_sellers_near · Private data: get_property, search_properties, find_owner_portfolio, search, fetch, find_entity_owner, motivated_sellers_near, draft_offer_letter · Public sink: get_market_stats, find_entity_owner · Destructive: list_saved_filters, get_usage

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
